vars.finding_body: The `--timeout` description says "Overall session timeout in seconds", but this flag accepts a Go duration (same as `avenor run` line 44: `30s`, `5m`, etc.). Passing a bare integer like `60` will not work as expected.

tests.description: avenor/34: WaitForDone subscription leak — fixed with scoped context

vars.finding_body: `WaitForDone` subscribes with `SubscribeRuntime(ctx, sessionID)` but never unsubscribes or closes the subscription after returning. This leaks subscriber resources on the client side over time.

discussion.author: sdougbrown
discussion.body: `👾 AI Agent` Fixed in 7e63102. `WaitForDone` now creates a scoped subscription context (`subCtx`) and calls `cancel()` on return, which unregisters/closes the runtime subscription promptly and avoids subscriber buildup.

tests.description: avenor/34: spawnAgents 'concurrently' vs sequential loop — design rationale

vars.finding_body: spawnAgentsTool runs agents sequentially in a for loop despite the description saying 'All agents run concurrently.'

discussion.author: sdougbrown
discussion.body: `👾 AI Agent` Leaving as-is by design. `spawn_agents` dispatches spawn RPCs sequentially, but each spawned runtime starts immediately and runs concurrently in the supervisor. The wording "run concurrently" describes runtime execution, not concurrent client-side RPC issuance.

tests.description: avenor/34: spawnAgents partial failure — accepted with follow-up tracking

vars.finding_body: `spawnAgentsTool.Execute` has partial failure semantics: if agent N fails to spawn, agents 0..N-1 are already spawned with no way to roll them back.

discussion.author: sdougbrown
discussion.body: `👾 AI Agent` Accepting as-is for this PR scope. Partial failure semantics in `spawn_agents` are currently intentional: each spawn is an independent RPC and previously spawned runtimes keep running. We can track rollback/cancellation semantics as a follow-up enhancement if desired.

tests.description: avenor/34: requestID timer closure — user claims false positive, accepted

vars.finding_body: Race condition in RuntimeSendToParent timer closure: the `requestID` variable is captured by reference in the `time.AfterFunc` closure.

discussion.author: sdougbrown
discussion.body: `👾 AI Agent` Leaving as-is. This is a false positive: `requestID` is function-local and not reassigned after creation. The timer closure captures that immutable value for this invocation, so there is no cross-request race from variable reuse.
